svg.title: SpecSpec interface detail: renderer messages, CLI processes, Python calls and agent use
svg.desc: A companion zoom to architecture.svg. The shared browser renderer calls the SpecSpecHost message and presentation-state port. Authorized VS Code or Electron adapters connect it to GraphSession, shared project reads and optional native document coordination and the bounded invoke subprocess bridge. The bridge starts a configured CLI executable with argument arrays, an explicit project root, shell false and UTF-8 stdin. A project-scoped API channel or ordinary CLI process contains both the Click CLI facade and the reusable domain library; the facade makes ordinary Python function calls and serializes results or SpecError diagnostics into an API 6 JSON envelope. The agent calls this same CLI contract directly from its own shell, bypassing UI messages and host queues. Alternative Python integrations import the same module code in their own process, using Python objects and exceptions rather than JSON. Payload examples distinguish renderer Save messages, translated CLI arguments and body stdin, and returned JSON plus exit status. A native form edit trace follows sequence-numbered input through API-6 native plan overlays, a non-writing before/after plan, guarded WorkspaceEdit application to a TextDocument and acknowledgement back to the renderer. Native Save writes files separately and can persist invalid text. A routing sidebar shows shared Electron/VS Code reads with optional overlays, commit targets, managed mutations and source previews. Host API channels are bounded child processes, with an independent warmed source-preview lane and fresh validation per frame.
svg.metadata: Descriptive documentation of current shortcut-free node format 6 and API 6. Self-contained offline SVG with system font fallbacks and local markers only. Companion overview: docs/architecture.svg. Guide and source links: docs/architecture.md. Payload snippets are illustrative; an empty result in the response example stands in for command-specific data.

g.text: UI messages become host commands. The CLI calls a Python library—not another service.
Numbered seams: 1 messages · 2 process I/O · 3 Python calls

Unprivileged shared renderer and SpecSpecHost message/state methods
g.text: Typed actions, node IDs and text

g.aria-label: Authorized host adapters, per-view GraphSession, per-project ProjectDocuments and bounded CLI bridge
g.text: Checks trust, IDs and form conflicts
Per project: overlays, plan / apply queue

g.aria-label: Contract one: host-neutral messages through VS Code webview messaging or Electron's scoped preload IPC
Project-scoped Python API channels or ordinary CLI processes; facade and library share each process
g.text: BOUNDED PYTHON API CHANNEL / ORDINARY CLI PROCESS

g.aria-label: Click parses inputs, dispatches ordinary Python calls and emits results or guarded diagnostics
Reusable domain functions and types; read/validation, non-writing plans, managed mutations and Git/source resolution share graph rules
Contract three: ordinary function calls return Python records or raise SpecError; no RPC or second process
Contract two: explicit root, shell-free argv and UTF-8 stdin in; versioned JSON and exit status out
The agent calls the same CLI directly, bypassing renderer messages and JavaScript host coordination
g.text: No UI port or built-in connector
Read: show / query / diff · write: add / update / delete · check [--staged]
Check stdout + exit status. --with-ancestors adds every matched node's complete parent paths.

g.aria-label: Alternative Python embedding imports the same modules in the caller's own process; it is not a connection to the CLI process
g.text: Same code in your process; objects / SpecError, not JSON.
Direct agent calls skip UI confirmation queues and VS Code dirty-buffer guards. The agent/harness owns its process controls.
CLI reads disk. VS Code supplies native document overlays. Project-scoped API channels reuse interpreter lifetime with fresh reads.

g.aria-label: Illustrative renderer Save message, translated process call and returned API envelope
g.text: The host translates. The CLI serializes.

g.aria-label: Contract one example: a managed Save message contains data, not arbitrary CLI commands
Contract two request: the host constructs update argv and sends raw body text on stdin
g.text: cwd=root · shell:false · UTF-8 stdin = body text
Bridge defaults: 120 s / 16 MiB combined stdout + stderr

g.aria-label: Contract two response: one JSON envelope on stdout plus the process exit status
g.text: Command-specific result omitted here as an empty object
Host rejects wrong API, malformed output, !ok or nonzero exit.

g.aria-label: A successful editor request may return an invalid snapshot; process success is not graph validity
g.text: A non-writing plan can preserve repairable invalid text. Native Save can persist it.
api stdin is JSON { api_version: 6, op, documents, edit? }, not raw body text. Diagnostics carry code, message, severity and optional path / node_id / line.

g.aria-label: Host results become UI snapshot or document-status events; a rendered token and visible membership acknowledge drawing
g.text: Host → UI: snapshot + diff + renderToken, or document-status + editSequence. UI → host: rendered (token + visible membership).

g.aria-label: Sequence trace of one VS Code form edit and its separate native file Save
g.text: A plan returns before a file is saved.
VS Code node-file form · ordinary managed Save routes are listed on the right.

g.aria-label: Renderer, shared host document coordination, Python editor command and VS Code native TextDocument
Sequence-numbered edit input is coalesced and bound to the current native resource
The host sends all open document overlays plus the requested edit on editor stdin
The CLI returns exact before/after text, snapshot and diagnostics to project-level coordination
The host checks version and before text, then applies a minimal WorkspaceEdit to the native document
g.text: Check version + before text → minimal WorkspaceEdit

g.aria-label: A matching document-status sequence acknowledgement returns to the renderer without clearing newer input
g.text: Dirty buffer · native undo / redo · split text shared

g.aria-label: Native Save or autosave persists the TextDocument to node files separately from Python; invalid text may be saved
g.text: No Python lock / journal; invalid text can be saved.
Typing is coalesced; version and sequence guards protect newer input. Raw text edits go straight to the TextDocument.

g.aria-label: Other UI routes choose different CLI commands and library paths according to view and persistence owner
g.text: Working first, then comparison · shared hints/cache
stdin: { documents } · no edit · no file write
workspace.py writer → lock / journal / saved files
VS Code first refuses dirty SpecSpec documents.
Capture returns a reference; the form's Save persists it.
